# Directional solution atlas

Model choices and proposed workflows are analyst hypotheses. This is not a final design or a claim about Razorpay’s internal models. Each original pain keeps its ID and priority.

## FAM-01 — Reorder timing and recent-purchase suppression

Shared customer/SKU history and a contact decision; solve timing and suppression together. Combine into one opportunity. Members: 09.2.1, 09.2.2, 09.2.4

## FAM-02 — Choosing whether to incentivise

Shared comparison of no action, reminder and approved incentive; the same experiment can address all three. Combine into one opportunity. Members: 09.3.2, 09.3.3, 09.5.3

## FAM-03 — Campaign incrementality and delayed effects

Shared exposure ledger and outcome window; use one measurement component. Combine into one opportunity. Members: 09.5.1, 09.5.2, 09.5.4

## 01.1.1 — My launch is ready but the payment account is not approved

**Approach:** LLM copilot / fixed workflow · Build on existing
**Family:** FAM-45 — Business eligibility and identity

**Candidate models:** Document extraction + grounded LLM
**Deep learning:** Use a pretrained LLM or OCR/document model; do not train a foundation model. Handwriting or image quality may require specialised OCR and review.
**Training data:** Authorised source documents, field schema, current policies and a reviewed set of correct field extractions. A pretrained model can start without merchant-specific training.
**Features:** Documents, category, identity, bank evidence and provider rejection reasons.
**Target:** The verified missing onboarding requirement or supported business eligibility. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Time to first live payment; launch days lost.
**Agent choice:** Language assistance; no dynamic agent required. Retrieval, extraction or drafting has a predictable path. Start with a reviewed model response; use an agent only if case-specific tool sequencing proves necessary.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Days at each activation stage; rejection reasons; resubmissions.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Documents, category, identity, bank evidence and provider rejection reasons.
3. Assess: Templates, keyword extraction and a human-reviewed checklist. Candidate target: The verified missing onboarding requirement or supported business eligibility. Use Document extraction + grounded LLM only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: An activation checklist with cited missing evidence, responsible party and next permitted submission. Specific need: See the missing requirement, responsible party and next step for my business type.
5. Review / change / approve: Review rejection evidence; correct documents/entity details; approve a submission.
6. Execute: a fixed workflow performs only the approved action; keep uncertain cases in a human queue.
7. Observe the outcome: Time to first live payment; launch days lost. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read submitted documents and provider status; prepare corrected checklist or approved submission.

**Merchant controls:** Review rejection evidence; correct documents/entity details; approve a submission.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Save corrected fields and error reasons as evaluation cases; improve retrieval, schemas and prompts under review. Fine-tune only if consented data and repeated errors justify it. Track the specific business outcome: Time to first live payment; launch days lost.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Measure field accuracy, source citation correctness and numeric consistency; route unreadable or contradictory documents to people.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Never invent identity evidence or bypass provider eligibility; unresolved identity mismatch goes to the provider. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Time to first live payment; launch days lost. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth.

**Evaluation:** Observe actual activation cases, avoid counting all delayed launches as lost sales.

**Razorpay direction:** Activation and identity workflow; the provider retains eligibility decisions.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. Confirm merchant eligibility, connector scopes and commercial/developer access; otherwise build the extension around permitted APIs or reviewed exports.

Evidence source IDs: R19, R20, A01, A09. See the source register in merchant-research.md.

5. Review / change / approve: Review rejection evidence; correct documents/entity details; approve a submission.

## 01.1.4 — Changing the owner, bank account or entity interrupts my trading

**Approach:** Rules / statistics / workflow · Extend existing
**Family:** FAM-73 — Changing the owner, bank account or entity interrupts my trading

**Candidate models:** Rules, state machine and verified calculations
**Deep learning:** No deep learning required. A language explanation could be optional; it must not determine financial facts.
**Training data:** No training set needed. Required inputs are current records, stable identifiers, policy versions and worked examples for acceptance tests.
**Features:** Documents, category, identity, bank evidence and provider rejection reasons.
**Target:** The verified missing onboarding requirement or supported business eligibility. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Downtime during business changes; time to restore access.

## 01.5.3 — Automation fails halfway and nobody owns the remaining work

**Approach:** Hybrid agent + rules · Extend existing
**Family:** FAM-26 — Partial failure and inconsistent systems

**Candidate models:** Grounded LLM diagnosis over deterministic queries; a grounded pretrained LLM may orchestrate the case, while state, permissions and financial calculations remain in code.
**Deep learning:** A pretrained LLM can coordinate queries. Anomaly models are optional after reliable instrumentation; no custom deep network is initially justified. Separately, the proposed agent orchestrator uses a pretrained LLM, which is itself deep learning; this does not require training a custom deep model for the merchant.
**Training data:** Linked events, timestamps, known incident cases, source definitions and read-only query tools; resolved cases provide evaluation labels.
**Features:** Evidence timestamps, tool calls, state transitions, action identifiers and rollback capabilities.
**Target:** An unsupported answer, policy breach or safely resumable partial run. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Time to recover; duplicate actions.
**Agent choice:** Candidate for bounded agent orchestration. The next information request or tool action can depend on an unexpected reply or intermediate result. A model may choose among approved tools, with a bounded case, cost/step budget and explicit stop state.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Failed actions; retry count; unresolved queue age.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Evidence timestamps, tool calls, state transitions, action identifiers and rollback capabilities.
3. Assess: Dashboards, SQL checks, incident playbooks and manual investigation. Candidate target: An unsupported answer, policy breach or safely resumable partial run. Use Grounded LLM diagnosis over deterministic queries only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A run-health or safety case with verified state, uncertainty, allowed recovery and a human escalation owner. Specific need: See partial completion, safe retry state and a named human handoff.
5. Review / change / approve: Review accessed fields, logs and policy checks; edit scopes/limits/owners; approve permission changes.
6. Execute: a bounded agent selects the next permitted tool from the case evidence; each write passes independent policy checks and required approval.
7. Observe the outcome: Time to recover; duplicate actions. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Inspect grants and run logs; preview a policy change; request scoped revoke/pause and verify acknowledgement.

**Merchant controls:** Review accessed fields, logs and policy checks; edit scopes/limits/owners; approve permission changes.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Store confirmed causes, rejected suggestions and tool traces; evaluate diagnosis and action-selection improvements on held-out incidents. Track the specific business outcome: Time to recover; duplicate actions.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Recompute all numbers in code; require source IDs for explanations, separate correlation from cause, and cap tool loops.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Enforce permissions outside the LLM; revocation and pause must be acknowledged by each connector, with a human owner for active runs. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Time to recover; duplicate actions. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth.

**Evaluation:** Use staged failures, correctness checks and manual handoff time; do not use sales as the primary metric.

**Razorpay direction:** Use documented boundaries as a starting point; cross-tool policy/partial-run control requires extra engineering.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. Confirm merchant eligibility, connector scopes and commercial/developer access; otherwise build the extension around permitted APIs or reviewed exports.

## 02.2.3 — Wholesale quotes ignore minimum quantities and special handling

**Approach:** Hybrid agent + rules · Adjacent / new workflow
**Family:** FAM-51 — Commercial quote economics

**Candidate models:** Document extraction + grounded LLM; a grounded pretrained LLM may orchestrate the case, while state, permissions and financial calculations remain in code.
**Deep learning:** Use a pretrained LLM or OCR/document model; do not train a foundation model. Handwriting or image quality may require specialised OCR and review. Separately, the proposed agent orchestrator uses a pretrained LLM, which is itself deep learning; this does not require training a custom deep model for the merchant.
**Training data:** Authorised source documents, field schema, current policies and a reviewed set of correct field extractions. A pretrained model can start without merchant-specific training.
**Features:** Cost components, price/quantity, compatibility, negotiated terms and plan usage.
**Target:** Feasible profitable price/bundle/quote or correct plan terms. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Quote-to-order margin; exceptions per quote.
**Agent choice:** Candidate for bounded agent orchestration. The next information request or tool action can depend on an unexpected reply or intermediate result. A model may choose among approved tools, with a bounded case, cost/step budget and explicit stop state.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Quote revisions; order size; special requests; payment terms.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Cost components, price/quantity, compatibility, negotiated terms and plan usage.
3. Assess: Templates, keyword extraction and a human-reviewed checklist. Candidate target: Feasible profitable price/bundle/quote or correct plan terms. Use Document extraction + grounded LLM only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A commercial-options comparison with explicit costs, margin floor and terms requiring approval. Specific need: Price order-specific packing, delivery and credit costs explicitly.
5. Review / change / approve: Review cost assumptions and proposed options; change margin floors, products or prices; approve a commercial change.
6. Execute: a bounded agent selects the next permitted tool from the case evidence; each write passes independent policy checks and required approval.
7. Observe the outcome: Quote-to-order margin; exceptions per quote. Verify any sales claim through incremental fulfilled contribution after costs. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read catalog/costs/stock; calculate options in code; draft a price, bundle or assortment change.

**Merchant controls:** Review cost assumptions and proposed options; change margin floors, products or prices; approve a commercial change.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Save corrected fields and error reasons as evaluation cases; improve retrieval, schemas and prompts under review. Fine-tune only if consented data and repeated errors justify it. Track the specific business outcome: Quote-to-order margin; exceptions per quote.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Measure field accuracy, source citation correctness and numeric consistency; route unreadable or contradictory documents to people.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Stale stock or incomplete cost data blocks publication; never silently change a price or contract. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Quote-to-order margin; exceptions per quote. Verify any sales claim through incremental fulfilled contribution after costs.

**Evaluation:** Track net contribution per fulfilled sale, cancellation and repeat demand.

**Razorpay direction:** Commercial economics and catalog decisions need a new connected merchant workflow.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. ## 02.3.1 — I discover a stockout only after customers try to buy

**Approach:** Predictive ML + workflow · Adjacent / new workflow
**Family:** FAM-05 — Supply-aware growth

**Candidate models:** Seasonal baseline → exponential smoothing or boosted-tree quantiles
**Deep learning:** Deep sequence models are a later option only if extensive diverse history beats simple baselines; small merchants rarely justify training one from scratch.
**Training data:** Consistent dated series, multiple relevant cycles, calendar effects, known commitments and past-only regressors. Stockouts or missing data must not be treated as zero demand.
**Features:** Sales and lost-demand indicators by SKU, lead times, reservations, seasonality and physical counts.
**Target:** SKU demand over replenishment lead time or accurate available-to-promise stock. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Stockout days; unfulfilled demand.
**Agent choice:** Model with a fixed workflow; agent optional. A prediction or ranking can feed a predetermined review-and-action path. Model uncertainty alone does not require an autonomous planner.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Available stock; sales velocity; lead-time variation.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Sales and lost-demand indicators by SKU, lead times, reservations, seasonality and physical counts.
3. Assess: Seasonal naive forecast plus merchant-entered scenario assumptions. Candidate target: SKU demand over replenishment lead time or accurate available-to-promise stock. Use Seasonal baseline → exponential smoothing or boosted-tree quantiles only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A stock-risk view with an uncertainty range and a proposed quantity/transfer or stock correction. Specific need: Anticipate replenishment using demand, supplier lead time and safety stock.
5. Review / change / approve: Review forecast range and stock ledger; edit service levels, lead times or reorder quantity; approve a purchase/transfer.
6. Execute: a fixed workflow performs only the approved action; keep uncertain cases in a human queue.
7. Observe the outcome: Incremental fulfilled contribution from fewer stockouts, net of extra inventory, expiry and financing costs. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read stock and demand history; run forecast/constraints; prepare a purchase or transfer request.

**Merchant controls:** Review forecast range and stock ledger; edit service levels, lead times or reorder quantity; approve a purchase/transfer.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Compare forecast with realised values through rolling time backtests; refresh approved models and show changing uncertainty. Track the specific business outcome: Stockout days; unfulfilled demand.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Track forecast error and interval coverage by horizon; separate forecast quality from the benefit of the action chosen.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Physical-count conflicts and supplier uncertainty route to operations; cap inventory exposure and preserve order commitments. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Incremental fulfilled contribution from fewer stockouts, net of extra inventory, expiry and financing costs.

**Evaluation:** Compare forecast and reorder decisions with a simple seasonal baseline; measure fulfilled demand and stock carrying cost.

**Razorpay direction:** Inventory and SKU replenishment are a new adjacent workflow requiring authoritative operating data.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. Confirm merchant eligibility, connector scopes and commercial/developer access; otherwise build the extension around permitted APIs or reviewed exports.

Evidence source IDs: R04, A06, A02. See the source register in merchant-research.md.

## 02.4.3 — The received batch is short or defective and evidence is scattered

**Approach:** Hybrid agent + rules · Extend existing
**Family:** FAM-54 — Purchasing evidence and obligations

6. Execute: a bounded agent selects the next permitted tool from the case evidence; each write passes independent policy checks and required approval.
7. Observe the outcome: Supplier credit recovered; defect resolution time. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

## 02.5.1 — A service slot appears available but the right employee is not

**Approach:** Rules / statistics / workflow · Adjacent / new workflow
**Family:** FAM-43 — Capacity-aware operating plan

**Candidate models:** Constraint solver / linear or integer optimization
**Deep learning:** No deep learning required. An LLM may explain a plan but should not be the solver.
**Training data:** Capacity, commitments, allowed options, objective costs and hard constraints; no training labels are needed.
**Features:** Skills, calendars, shifts, resource constraints and completed/cancelled bookings.
**Target:** Feasible capacity and expected fulfilled demand in a time window. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Double bookings; rescheduling rate.
**Agent choice:** No agent required for the core job. The core computation or transition is well specified. Use deterministic automation or analysis; add a language copilot only if it measurably reduces exception-handling effort.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Staff skills; working hours; room/equipment availability.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Skills, calendars, shifts, resource constraints and completed/cancelled bookings.
3. Assess: Explicit business rules and a feasible manually reviewed schedule or allocation. Candidate target: Feasible capacity and expected fulfilled demand in a time window. Use Constraint solver / linear or integer optimization only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A feasible capacity plan or limited demand experiment, with constraints and expected economics visible. Specific need: Match bookings to skills, calendars and required resources.
5. Review / change / approve: Review demand and capacity; edit staffing, constraints or offer windows; approve schedule or capacity changes.
6. Execute: a fixed workflow performs only the approved action; keep uncertain cases in a human queue.
7. Observe the outcome: Double bookings; rescheduling rate. Verify any sales claim through incremental fulfilled contribution after costs. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read capacity/calendar; run a constraint solver; prepare an approved schedule or offer-window change.

Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Compare planned and actual outcomes; correct input estimates and approved constraints. Any demand predictor is a separate model. Track the specific business outcome: Double bookings; rescheduling rate.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Check feasibility, constraint violations and realised cost; show when no feasible solution exists instead of silently relaxing limits.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Do not relax skills, hours or safety constraints silently; unavailable capacity returns a no-feasible-plan result. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Double bookings; rescheduling rate. Verify any sales claim through incremental fulfilled contribution after costs.

## 04.1.1 — Customers cannot select the right size, scent, quantity or service

**Approach:** Hybrid agent + rules · Adjacent / new workflow
**Family:** FAM-41 — Configuration and sensible expansion

**Candidate models:** Attribute matching → learning-to-rank; a grounded pretrained LLM may orchestrate the case, while state, permissions and financial calculations remain in code.
**Deep learning:** Pretrained embeddings may help interpret text. A deep recommender needs extensive interaction data and is not the initial requirement. Separately, the proposed agent orchestrator uses a pretrained LLM, which is itself deep learning; this does not require training a custom deep model for the merchant.
**Training data:** Candidate items, eligibility, stock, customer-stated needs, recorded exposures and eventual purchase/return outcomes. Ranking training needs grouped candidates and relevance labels.
**Features:** Customer-stated needs, allowed variants, quote terms, inventory and calendar availability.
**Target:** Suitable order configuration, agreed quote or feasible appointment. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Order completion; wrong-variant returns.
**Agent choice:** Candidate for bounded agent orchestration. The next information request or tool action can depend on an unexpected reply or intermediate result. A model may choose among approved tools, with a bounded case, cost/step budget and explicit stop state.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Variant changes; help requests; configuration errors.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Customer-stated needs, allowed variants, quote terms, inventory and calendar availability.
3. Assess: Verified product/offer attributes and merchant-approved compatibility rules. Candidate target: Suitable order configuration, agreed quote or feasible appointment. Use Attribute matching → learning-to-rank only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A feasible product/quote/slot option that preserves the customer’s selections and records agreed terms. Specific need: Explain options and validate combinations before the order is placed.
5. Review / change / approve: Review affected funnel/options; edit policy wording and allowed terms; approve a checkout experiment or change.
6. Execute: a bounded agent selects the next permitted tool from the case evidence; each write passes independent policy checks and required approval.
7. Observe the outcome: Order completion; wrong-variant returns. Verify any sales claim through incremental fulfilled contribution after costs. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read funnel and eligible options; validate policy/amount; prepare a controlled checkout change.

**Merchant controls:** Review affected funnel/options; edit policy wording and allowed terms; approve a checkout experiment or change.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Collect accepted/rejected options and later returns; evaluate rankings and incremental outcome against the rules baseline. Track the specific business outcome: Order completion; wrong-variant returns.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Check stock and suitability before ranking; assess ranking quality alongside fulfilment, contribution and wrong recommendations.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Maintain accurate total price and accessible purchase path; revert a change if correctness or conversion guardrails fail. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Order completion; wrong-variant returns. Verify any sales claim through incremental fulfilled contribution after costs.

**Evaluation:** Compare accepted, fulfilled orders and contribution; track wrong recommendations and cancellations.

Track the specific business outcome: Promise-related abandonment; late commitments.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. ## 04.5.1 — I treat every abandoned cart as money that can be recovered

**Approach:** Hybrid agent + rules · Extend existing
**Family:** FAM-08 — Understanding abandoned intent

**Candidate models:** Logistic regression → calibrated gradient-boosted trees; a grounded pretrained LLM may orchestrate the case, while state, permissions and financial calculations remain in code.
**Deep learning:** Tabular ML is the first candidate. Deep learning is optional only if richer sequences or unstructured inputs add validated value at sufficient scale. Separately, the proposed agent orchestrator uses a pretrained LLM, which is itself deep learning; this does not require training a custom deep model for the merchant.
**Training data:** One row per eligible case at decision time; past-only features; actual positive/negative outcomes after a fixed observation window; actions and costs logged separately.
**Features:** Cart contents, current cross-channel order state, consent, outreach cost and approved offers.
**Target:** Eligible abandoned intent, incremental action benefit or contact suppression. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Recovery eligibility accuracy; wasted contacts.
**Agent choice:** Candidate for bounded agent orchestration. The next information request or tool action can depend on an unexpected reply or intermediate result. A model may choose among approved tools, with a bounded case, cost/step budget and explicit stop state.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Abandonment stage; payment attempts; customer response.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Cart contents, current cross-channel order state, consent, outreach cost and approved offers.
3. Assess: Reason codes and a simple segment-specific decision rule. Candidate target: Eligible abandoned intent, incremental action benefit or contact suppression. Use Logistic regression → calibrated gradient-boosted trees only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A cart case with current eligibility, likely blocker, no-action option and a permitted response draft. Specific need: Separate browsing, price comparison, technical friction and genuine intent.
5. Review / change / approve: Review cart state, intent evidence and message; edit allowed offers/contact window; approve outreach or a bounded campaign.
6. Execute: a bounded agent selects the next permitted tool from the case evidence; each write passes independent policy checks and required approval.
7. Observe the outcome: Recovery eligibility accuracy; wasted contacts. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read cart/current orders, stock and consent; fetch approved offers; draft outreach/payment-link request; log result.

**Merchant controls:** Review cart state, intent evidence and message; edit allowed offers/contact window; approve outreach or a bounded campaign.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Retrain in approved batches on matured labels; use time-based holdouts, calibration and drift monitoring. Prediction of response is not proof of incremental effect. Track the specific business outcome: Recovery eligibility accuracy; wasted contacts.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Evaluate precision/recall at action capacity, probability calibration and net decision value; audit selection bias and differences across merchant segments.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Check purchase status immediately before send; suppress duplicate contact, opt-outs and unavailable items; no invented scarcity or discounts. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Recovery eligibility accuracy; wasted contacts. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals.

**Evaluation:** Randomize eligible abandoned carts against no contact; subtract discounts, contact costs and later refunds.

**Razorpay direction:** Existing cart agent and approved offers; investigate better qualification, action selection and net impact.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. Confirm merchant eligibility, connector scopes and commercial/developer access; otherwise build the extension around permitted APIs or reviewed exports.

## 04.5.4 — Several tools contact the same person repeatedly

**Approach:** Rules / statistics / workflow · Extend existing
**Family:** FAM-09 — Avoid redundant recovery contact

**Candidate models:** Rules, state machine and verified calculations
**Deep learning:** No deep learning required. A language explanation could be optional; it must not determine financial facts.
**Training data:** No training set needed. Required inputs are current records, stable identifiers, policy versions and worked examples for acceptance tests.
**Features:** Cart contents, current cross-channel order state, consent, outreach cost and approved offers.
**Target:** Eligible abandoned intent, incremental action benefit or contact suppression. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Duplicate outreach; net recovery after contact costs.
**Agent choice:** No agent required for the core job. The core computation or transition is well specified. Use deterministic automation or analysis; add a language copilot only if it measurably reduces exception-handling effort.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Cross-tool contact history; opt-out; purchase completion.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Cart contents, current cross-channel order state, consent, outreach cost and approved offers.
3. Assess: Explicit conditions, authoritative status checks and a human exception queue. Candidate target: Eligible abandoned intent, incremental action benefit or contact suppression. Use Rules, state machine and verified calculations only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A cart case with current eligibility, likely blocker, no-action option and a permitted response draft. Specific need: Coordinate contact timing, consent, frequency and stopping conditions.
5. Review / change / approve: Review cart state, intent evidence and message; edit allowed offers/contact window; approve outreach or a bounded campaign.
6. Execute: a fixed workflow performs only the approved action; keep uncertain cases in a human queue.
7. Observe the outcome: Duplicate outreach; net recovery after contact costs. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read cart/current orders, stock and consent; fetch approved offers; draft outreach/payment-link request; log result.

**Merchant controls:** Review cart state, intent evidence and message; edit allowed offers/contact window; approve outreach or a bounded campaign.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Log exceptions and merchant corrections; propose versioned rule changes for approval. The system does not automatically train itself. **Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

## 05.1.1 — A bank or payment route fails even though the buyer wants to pay

**Approach:** Predictive ML + workflow · Build on existing
**Family:** FAM-48 — Payment path alternatives

**Candidate models:** Logistic regression → calibrated gradient-boosted trees
**Deep learning:** Tabular ML is the first candidate. Deep learning is optional only if richer sequences or unstructured inputs add validated value at sufficient scale.
**Training data:** One row per eligible case at decision time; past-only features; actual positive/negative outcomes after a fixed observation window; actions and costs logged separately.
**Features:** Provider failure codes, route availability, method eligibility and reconciled obligation state.
**Target:** Payment failure reason and permitted alternative path. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Payment success rate; unique orders recovered.
**Agent choice:** Model with a fixed workflow; agent optional. A prediction or ranking can feed a predetermined review-and-action path. Model uncertainty alone does not require an autonomous planner.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Failure codes; issuer/method/time success; provider health.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Provider failure codes, route availability, method eligibility and reconciled obligation state.
3. Assess: Reason codes and a simple segment-specific decision rule. Candidate target: Payment failure reason and permitted alternative path. Use Logistic regression → calibrated gradient-boosted trees only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A verified failure explanation and supported next payment option, with no duplicate obligation. Specific need: Identify the failing route and offer a supported alternative safely.
5. Review / change / approve: Review authoritative payment status and reason; edit allowed routes/attempt caps; approve permitted retry/capture steps.
6. Execute: a fixed workflow performs only the approved action; keep uncertain cases in a human queue.
7. Observe the outcome: Payment success rate; unique orders recovered. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read authoritative payment and obligation state; fetch supported methods; request only a permitted verified payment action.

**Merchant controls:** Review authoritative payment status and reason; edit allowed routes/attempt caps; approve permitted retry/capture steps.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Retrain in approved batches on matured labels; use time-based holdouts, calibration and drift monitoring. Prediction of response is not proof of incremental effect. Track the specific business outcome: Payment success rate; unique orders recovered.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Evaluate precision/recall at action capacity, probability calibration and net decision value; audit selection bias and differences across merchant segments.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Never retry an ambiguous debit blindly; verify mandate/authentication, use obligation IDs and reconcile before another attempt. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Payment success rate; unique orders recovered. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals.

**Evaluation:** Compare unique completed obligations against the existing routing baseline; avoid duplicate charges.

**Razorpay direction:** Existing payment execution and routing are the first building blocks; model-driven UX is optional.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. Confirm merchant eligibility, connector scopes and commercial/developer access; otherwise build the extension around permitted APIs or reviewed exports.

Evidence source IDs: R11, R17, A02, A03. See the source register in merchant-research.md.

## 05.4.3 — A customer makes a part-payment without explaining the deduction

**Approach:** Hybrid agent + rules · Extend existing
**Family:** FAM-07 — B2B deduction and dispute resolution

Separately, the proposed agent orchestrator uses a pretrained LLM, which is itself deep learning; this does not require training a custom deep model for the merchant.
**Training data:** Authorised source documents, field schema, current policies and a reviewed set of correct field extractions. A pretrained model can start without merchant-specific training.
**Features:** Invoices, due dates, receipts, customer contacts, remittance advice, acceptance and dispute threads.
**Target:** Valid outstanding balance, reason for deduction and correct collection owner. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Unresolved deductions; collection accuracy.
**Agent choice:** Candidate for bounded agent orchestration. The next information request or tool action can depend on an unexpected reply or intermediate result. A model may choose among approved tools, with a bounded case, cost/step budget and explicit stop state.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Invoice balance; remittance details; credits; withholding.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Invoices, due dates, receipts, customer contacts, remittance advice, acceptance and dispute threads.
3. Assess: Templates, keyword extraction and a human-reviewed checklist. Candidate target: Valid outstanding balance, reason for deduction and correct collection owner. Use Document extraction + grounded LLM only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A receivable case showing valid outstanding balance, deduction/dispute evidence, correct owner and draft next step. Specific need: Assemble a short-payment case, explain the remaining valid balance and draft a reason-specific next step.
5. Review / change / approve: Review invoice, deduction evidence and contact; correct balance/owner; approve message, revised terms or escalation.
6. Execute: a bounded agent selects the next permitted tool from the case evidence; each write passes independent policy checks and required approval.
7. Observe the outcome: Valid disputed balance collected less effort/cost; track days to resolution separately from revenue recognised. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read invoices/receipts, acceptance and correspondence; calculate valid balance; request missing evidence or draft a collection reply.

**Merchant controls:** Review invoice, deduction evidence and contact; correct balance/owner; approve message, revised terms or escalation.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Save corrected fields and error reasons as evaluation cases; improve retrieval, schemas and prompts under review. Fine-tune only if consented data and repeated errors justify it. Track the specific business outcome: Unresolved deductions; collection accuracy.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Measure field accuracy, source citation correctness and numeric consistency; route unreadable or contradictory documents to people.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Do not collect valid tax withholding or a settled balance; pause disputed amounts and reconcile partial payments before contact. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Valid disputed balance collected less effort/cost; track days to resolution separately from revenue recognised.

**Evaluation:** Measure valid outstanding value collected and days to resolution; separate cash acceleration from incremental revenue.

## 06.5.1 — A customer does not show up and the reserved slot is wasted

**Approach:** Hybrid agent + rules · Adjacent / new workflow
**Family:** FAM-42 — Feasible booking and no-show handling

**Candidate models:** Logistic regression → calibrated gradient-boosted trees; a grounded pretrained LLM may orchestrate the case, while state, permissions and financial calculations remain in code.
**Deep learning:** Tabular ML is the first candidate. Deep learning is optional only if richer sequences or unstructured inputs add validated value at sufficient scale. Separately, the proposed agent orchestrator uses a pretrained LLM, which is itself deep learning; this does not require training a custom deep model for the merchant.
**Training data:** One row per eligible case at decision time; past-only features; actual positive/negative outcomes after a fixed observation window; actions and costs logged separately.
**Features:** Booking history, cancellation reasons, staff availability, payments, entitlement and delivery proof.
**Target:** Kept/rescheduled appointment, entitlement repair or verified milestone acceptance. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: No-show rate; recovered capacity.
**Agent choice:** Candidate for bounded agent orchestration. The next information request or tool action can depend on an unexpected reply or intermediate result. A model may choose among approved tools, with a bounded case, cost/step budget and explicit stop state.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Attendance; reminder response; cancellation time.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Booking history, cancellation reasons, staff availability, payments, entitlement and delivery proof.
3. Assess: Reason codes and a simple segment-specific decision rule. Candidate target: Kept/rescheduled appointment, entitlement repair or verified milestone acceptance. Use Logistic regression → calibrated gradient-boosted trees only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A booking, entitlement or acceptance case with the agreed obligation and a reviewable repair/reschedule step. Specific need: Confirm appointments, offer rescheduling and apply disclosed policies.
5. Review / change / approve: Review booking, entitlement or acceptance evidence; change eligible slot/owner; approve rescheduling or service-state repair.
6. Execute: a bounded agent selects the next permitted tool from the case evidence; each write passes independent policy checks and required approval.
7. Observe the outcome: No-show rate; recovered capacity. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read booking/payment/entitlement; verify availability; prepare an approved reschedule or state correction.

**Merchant controls:** Review booking, entitlement or acceptance evidence; change eligible slot/owner; approve rescheduling or service-state repair.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Retrain in approved batches on matured labels; use time-based holdouts, calibration and drift monitoring. Prediction of response is not proof of incremental effect. Track the specific business outcome: No-show rate; recovered capacity.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Evaluate precision/recall at action capacity, probability calibration and net decision value; audit selection bias and differences across merchant segments.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** No double-booking or duplicate entitlement grant; preserve disclosed cancellation terms and current customer consent. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** No-show rate; recovered capacity. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals.

**Evaluation:** Measure kept/rescheduled appointments or fulfilled paid obligations without double-counting deposits.

**Razorpay direction:** Booking, entitlement and B2B acceptance tools are external dependencies; the solution would be adjacent.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. ### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Return reason; replacement stock; exchange acceptance.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Return intent, stock, paid allocations, suitability, shipping cost and refund rights.

5. Review / change / approve: Review reason, stock, policy and economics; edit eligible exchange options; approve contact or case action.
6. Execute: a bounded agent selects the next permitted tool from the case evidence; each write passes independent policy checks and required approval.
7. Observe the outcome: Net value retained after exchange costs. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

## 07.3.4 — A refund approval waits because the merchant fears abuse

**Approach:** Predictive ML + workflow · Build on existing
**Family:** FAM-36 — Refund evidence and status

**Candidate models:** Calibrated logistic/boosted-tree risk model + human review
**Deep learning:** Sequence/graph deep learning is optional at scale; access to justified data and specialist validation comes first.
**Training data:** Permitted transaction features, confirmed mature fraud/legitimate outcomes, intervention history and chargeback delays. Declined cases lack fully observed counterfactual outcomes.
**Features:** Original payments, partial-item allocation, previous refunds, case identity and processor references.
**Target:** Correct refund amount/state or case requiring evidence review. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Time to refund; manual review yield.
**Agent choice:** Model with a fixed workflow; agent optional. A prediction or ranking can feed a predetermined review-and-action path. Model uncertainty alone does not require an autonomous planner.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Policy eligibility; risk signals; approval queue.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Original payments, partial-item allocation, previous refunds, case identity and processor references.
3. Assess: Existing provider risk system, known rules and an explicit review policy. Candidate target: Correct refund amount/state or case requiring evidence review. Use Calibrated logistic/boosted-tree risk model + human review only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A refund preview with verified eligibility, amount, prior actions and processor status. Specific need: Separate routine eligible refunds from cases needing evidence or approval.
5. Review / change / approve: Review original paid allocation, eligibility and prior refund; edit case metadata; approve the verified refund amount.
6. Execute: a fixed workflow performs only the approved action; keep uncertain cases in a human queue.
7. Observe the outcome: Time to refund; manual review yield. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read original payment and previous refund; calculate verified amount; request an approved refund and poll authoritative status.

**Merchant controls:** Review original paid allocation, eligibility and prior refund; edit case metadata; approve the verified refund amount.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Refresh after label maturity; monitor false declines, calibration and drift. Review distribution changes before relaxing any controls. Track the specific business outcome: Time to refund; manual review yield.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Evaluate loss and legitimate conversion jointly; challenge labels, selection bias and false-positive costs. An LLM is not a fraud truth detector.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Exact arithmetic, limits and duplicate checks are deterministic; unknown processor state stops another refund. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Time to refund; manual review yield. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth.

**Evaluation:** Measure accurate timely refunds, duplicates and support effort; never count delayed refunds as recovered revenue.

**Razorpay direction:** Use existing refund/status workflows before adding optional evidence interpretation.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. Confirm merchant eligibility, connector scopes and commercial/developer access; otherwise build the extension around permitted APIs or reviewed exports.

Evidence source IDs: R01, R18, A02, A03. See the source register in merchant-research.md.

## 08.2.3 — Refunds and disputes appear in a later period than the sale

**Approach:** Rules / statistics / workflow · Extend existing
**Family:** FAM-33 — Reconciliation across periods and formats

**Candidate models:** Deterministic matching + optional probabilistic record linkage
**Deep learning:** No deep learning for exact matching. Pretrained extraction/embeddings may help heterogeneous documents; arithmetic remains deterministic.
**Training data:** Authoritative records from both systems, stable identifiers, matching rules and reviewed correct/incorrect matches for any learned matcher.
**Features:** Record IDs, amounts, dates, currencies, source schemas and reviewed match examples.
**Target:** Verified match between bank, invoice, settlement and reversal records. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Unexplained period differences; adjustment accuracy.
**Agent choice:** No agent required for the core job. The core computation or transition is well specified. Use deterministic automation or analysis; add a language copilot only if it measurably reduces exception-handling effort.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Original IDs; reversal dates; settlement adjustments.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Record IDs, amounts, dates, currencies, source schemas and reviewed match examples.
3. Assess: Exact IDs, amount/date tolerances and an unmatched-record queue. Candidate target: Verified match between bank, invoice, settlement and reversal records. Use Deterministic matching + optional probabilistic record linkage only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A proposed match or unresolved exception with source records and a reversible ledger decision. Specific need: Link reversals to originals while preserving accounting dates.
5. Review / change / approve: Review proposed matches and totals; correct mapping/tolerance; approve ambiguous joins or ledger write.
6. Execute: a fixed workflow performs only the approved action; keep uncertain cases in a human queue.
7. Observe the outcome: Unexplained period differences; adjustment accuracy. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read source records; execute deterministic joins; propose ambiguous matches; request approval for ledger writes.

**Merchant controls:** Review proposed matches and totals; correct mapping/tolerance; approve ambiguous joins or ledger write.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Review false matches and unmatched patterns; change mapping rules under version control. Learn match weights only with labelled examples. Track the specific business outcome: Unexplained period differences; adjustment accuracy.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Optimise false-match precision before coverage; never auto-close an ambiguous financial difference.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** False matches are worse than unresolved items; preserve source records and reversible mapping history. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Unexplained period differences; adjustment accuracy. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth.

**Evaluation:** Measure matching accuracy, unresolved value and close time; do not count a match as new revenue.

**Razorpay direction:** Reporting/matching capabilities exist; irregular external records and exception handling need validation.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. Confirm merchant eligibility, connector scopes and commercial/developer access; otherwise build the extension around permitted APIs or reviewed exports.

Evidence source IDs: R01, R14, R05, R20, A03. See the source register in merchant-research.md.

## 08.5.1 — Two dashboards report different revenue for the same period

**Approach:** LLM copilot / fixed workflow · Extend existing
**Family:** FAM-12 — Explaining merchant performance

**Candidate models:** Grounded LLM diagnosis over deterministic queries
**Deep learning:** A pretrained LLM can coordinate queries. Anomaly models are optional after reliable instrumentation; no custom deep network is initially justified.
**Training data:** Linked events, timestamps, known incident cases, source definitions and read-only query tools; resolved cases provide evaluation labels.
**Features:** Versioned metric definitions, transaction events, stage funnels, reversals and allocated costs.
**Target:** Reproducible revenue/contribution definition or supported candidate cause of a change. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Reporting variance; reconciliation effort.
**Agent choice:** Language assistance; no dynamic agent required. Retrieval, extraction or drafting has a predictable path. Start with a reviewed model response; use an agent only if case-specific tool sequencing proves necessary.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Metric definitions; date ranges; included statuses.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Versioned metric definitions, transaction events, stage funnels, reversals and allocated costs.
3. Assess: Dashboards, SQL checks, incident playbooks and manual investigation. Candidate target: Reproducible revenue/contribution definition or supported candidate cause of a change. Use Grounded LLM diagnosis over deterministic queries only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A reproducible metric explanation or diagnostic brief with exact formulas, sources and missing inputs. Specific need: Expose definitions, time zones, taxes, refunds and recognition basis.
5. Review / change / approve: Review source rows, formula and timestamps; change window/definitions/cost allocation; approve any downstream action separately.
6. Execute: present the analysis or draft; a person initiates any external action in the appropriate system.
7. Observe the outcome: Reporting variance; reconciliation effort. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Run read-only parameterised queries and calculators; retrieve source records; produce cited analysis.

**Merchant controls:** Review source rows, formula and timestamps; change window/definitions/cost allocation; approve any downstream action separately.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Store confirmed causes, rejected suggestions and tool traces; evaluate diagnosis and action-selection improvements on held-out incidents. Track the specific business outcome: Reporting variance; reconciliation effort.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Recompute all numbers in code; require source IDs for explanations, separate correlation from cause, and cap tool loops.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Block unsupported causal narratives; recompute numbers and show missing data, not fabricated certainty. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Reporting variance; reconciliation effort. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth.

**Evaluation:** Validate diagnosis against known incidents and contribution completeness before attributing any downstream lift.

## 09.2.1 — I do not know when a customer is likely to need the product again

**Approach:** Predictive ML + workflow · Extend existing
**Family:** FAM-01 — Reorder timing and recent-purchase suppression

**Candidate models:** Cox proportional hazards or survival forest
**Deep learning:** No deep learning needed initially. Neural survival or sequence models require more history and a demonstrated improvement.
**Training data:** Purchase or obligation start times, follow-up end time, event occurrence, past features and customers with no observed next event. Right-censored cases must remain in the dataset.
**Features:** SKU purchase dates, observation windows, censored non-repeaters, stock, complaints and consent.
**Target:** Reorder window, likely lapse reason or no-contact eligibility. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Incremental repeat contribution; timing accuracy.
**Agent choice:** Model with a fixed workflow; agent optional. A prediction or ranking can feed a predetermined review-and-action path. Model uncertainty alone does not require an autonomous planner.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Order intervals; product/quantity; seasonality.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. SKU purchase dates, observation windows, censored non-repeaters, stock, complaints and consent.
3. Assess: Median repeat interval by product/cohort, with a broad uncertainty window. Candidate target: Reorder window, likely lapse reason or no-contact eligibility. Use Cox proportional hazards or survival forest only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A customer/product contact queue with an estimated need window, uncertainty and a do-not-contact reason. Specific need: Offer a reviewed reorder recommendation at an estimated need window, with suppression after a recent purchase.
5. Review / change / approve: Review cohort, need window and message; change timing, offers, exclusions and experiment size; approve outreach policy.
6. Execute: a fixed workflow performs only the approved action; keep uncertain cases in a human queue.
7. Observe the outcome: Incremental fulfilled contribution per eligible customer versus fixed-timing outreach; opt-outs and repeat rate as guardrails. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read consented purchase history, inventory and complaints; estimate window/action value; prepare outreach and record assignment/outcome.

**Merchant controls:** Review cohort, need window and message; change timing, offers, exclusions and experiment size; approve outreach policy.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Update with completed observation windows; backtest later cohorts and monitor timing calibration. Evaluate intervention lift separately from event prediction. Track the specific business outcome: Incremental repeat contribution; timing accuracy.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Check censoring assumptions, calibration by horizon, seasonal shifts and performance versus cohort intervals.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Verify consent and recent purchases before send; cap incentive/contact cost; preserve holdout and stop when opt-outs or harm rise. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Incremental fulfilled contribution per eligible customer versus fixed-timing outreach; opt-outs and repeat rate as guardrails.

**Evaluation:** Randomize eligible customers versus the existing journey; measure incremental fulfilled contribution and opt-outs.

**Razorpay direction:** Journeys, segments and recommendations exist; per-customer timing or causal incentive choice is proposed.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio.
