## 09.4.1 — A subscriber cancels because they need a pause, not a permanent exit

**Approach:** Hybrid agent + rules · Extend existing
**Family:** FAM-15 — Subscription retention and safe renewal

**Candidate models:** Grounded language model with current source retrieval; a grounded pretrained LLM may orchestrate the case, while state, permissions and financial calculations remain in code.
**Deep learning:** A pretrained LLM is sufficient initially. Retrieval adds current facts without requiring model training on merchant transactions. Separately, the proposed agent orchestrator uses a pretrained LLM, which is itself deep learning; this does not require training a custom deep model for the merchant.
**Training data:** Versioned product/policy content, permitted customer context, source freshness and a reviewed set of representative questions and answers.
**Features:** Reasons for cancellation, usage, account cadence, prior orders and authorised plan/offer options.
**Target:** Appropriate retention/expansion option or meaningful account-decline signal. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Retained value after costs; later satisfaction.
**Agent choice:** Candidate for bounded agent orchestration. The next information request or tool action can depend on an unexpected reply or intermediate result. A model may choose among approved tools, with a bounded case, cost/step budget and explicit stop state.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Cancellation reason; usage; billing cycle.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Reasons for cancellation, usage, account cadence, prior orders and authorised plan/offer options.
3. Assess: Approved templates, FAQ search or a guided form. Candidate target: Appropriate retention/expansion option or meaningful account-decline signal. Use Grounded language model with current source retrieval only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A relationship case with the observed change, customer-stated need and suitable pause/retention/expansion options. Specific need: Offer an appropriate approved pause or plan option with a clear cancel route.
5. Review / change / approve: Review mandate, cancellation/usage and proposed option; edit cadence/approved plans; approve outreach or allowed retry.
6. Execute: a bounded agent selects the next permitted tool from the case evidence; each write passes independent policy checks and required approval.
7. Observe the outcome: Retained value after costs; later satisfaction. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read mandate/plan/entitlement; reconcile receipts; draft contact or request an authorised retry/plan change.

**Merchant controls:** Review mandate, cancellation/usage and proposed option; edit cadence/approved plans; approve outreach or allowed retry.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Review correction categories and unresolved questions; update approved knowledge and evaluate prompt changes before release. Track the specific business outcome: Retained value after costs; later satisfaction.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Test answer correctness, unsupported claims, retrieval coverage and refusal/escalation behaviour; documents and customer messages are untrusted input.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Do not renew after cancellation or charge the wrong plan; verify customer choice and payment state before any debit or entitlement change. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Retained value after costs; later satisfaction. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals.

**Evaluation:** Measure retained paid relationships or useful expansion after costs; report cancellations and complaints.

**Razorpay direction:** Recovery and cancellation alternatives are described; confirm supported methods and entitlement integrations.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. Confirm merchant eligibility, connector scopes and commercial/developer access; otherwise build the extension around permitted APIs or reviewed exports.

## 10.1.1 — I have money across accounts but no reliable available-cash view

**Approach:** Rules / statistics / workflow · Extend existing
**Family:** FAM-23 — Cash visibility and reserves

**Candidate models:** Rules, state machine and verified calculations
**Deep learning:** No deep learning required. A language explanation could be optional; it must not determine financial facts.
**Training data:** No training set needed. Required inputs are current records, stable identifiers, policy versions and worked examples for acceptance tests.
**Features:** Bank balances, restrictions, payable dates, uncertain receivables, returns and planned commitments.
**Target:** Usable cash, timing shortfall or downside-aware commitment feasibility. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Available-cash accuracy; unexpected shortfalls.
**Agent choice:** No agent required for the core job. The core computation or transition is well specified. Use deterministic automation or analysis; add a language copilot only if it measurably reduces exception-handling effort.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Bank balances; pending payments; reserves; scheduled payouts.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Bank balances, restrictions, payable dates, uncertain receivables, returns and planned commitments.
3. Assess: Explicit conditions, authoritative status checks and a human exception queue. Candidate target: Usable cash, timing shortfall or downside-aware commitment feasibility. Use Rules, state machine and verified calculations only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A cash/commitment scenario with usable funds, uncertain timings and a reviewed financing or payment decision. Specific need: Combine usable balances and identify restricted or already-committed funds.
5. Review / change / approve: Review usable balances and scenarios; change assumptions, reserves and priorities; approve commitments or payments separately.
6. Execute: a fixed workflow performs only the approved action; keep uncertain cases in a human queue.
7. Observe the outcome: Available-cash accuracy; unexpected shortfalls. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read balances/obligations; run scenarios; prepare priorities; require independent approval for any payment or contract action.

**Merchant controls:** Review usable balances and scenarios; change assumptions, reserves and priorities; approve commitments or payments separately.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

Track the specific business outcome: Available-cash accuracy; unexpected shortfalls.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Test invariants, duplicate events, stale records, partial failures and boundary amounts. Compare exact outputs with independently verified examples.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Never infer guaranteed inflows, move cash or cancel contracts without authority; show downside and restricted funds. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Available-cash accuracy; unexpected shortfalls. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth.

**Evaluation:** Measure forecast error and missed obligations; a financed new order is growth only after fulfilment and costs.

5. Review / change / approve: Review usable balances and scenarios; change assumptions, reserves and priorities; approve commitments or payments separately.
6. Execute: a bounded agent selects the next permitted tool from the case evidence; each write passes independent policy checks and required approval.
7. Observe the outcome: Cash shortfall days; forecast error. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Training data:** Consistent dated series, multiple relevant cycles, calendar effects, known commitments and past-only regressors. Stockouts or missing data must not be treated as zero demand.
**Features:** Bank balances, restrictions, payable dates, uncertain receivables, returns and planned commitments.
**Target:** Usable cash, timing shortfall or downside-aware commitment feasibility. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Forecast resilience; avoided emergency borrowing.
**Agent choice:** Model with a fixed workflow; agent optional. A prediction or ranking can feed a predetermined review-and-action path. Model uncertainty alone does not require an autonomous planner.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Delay distributions; refund patterns; demand scenarios.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Bank balances, restrictions, payable dates, uncertain receivables, returns and planned commitments.
3. Assess: Seasonal naive forecast plus merchant-entered scenario assumptions. Candidate target: Usable cash, timing shortfall or downside-aware commitment feasibility. Use Seasonal baseline → exponential smoothing or boosted-tree quantiles only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A cash/commitment scenario with usable funds, uncertain timings and a reviewed financing or payment decision. Specific need: Stress-test realistic downside cases and show assumptions.
5. Review / change / approve: Review usable balances and scenarios; change assumptions, reserves and priorities; approve commitments or payments separately.
6. Execute: present the analysis or draft; a person initiates any external action in the appropriate system.
7. Observe the outcome: Forecast error by horizon, missed obligations and financing cost; no sales-growth claim. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read balances/obligations; run scenarios; prepare priorities; require independent approval for any payment or contract action.

**Merchant controls:** Review usable balances and scenarios; change assumptions, reserves and priorities; approve commitments or payments separately.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Compare forecast with realised values through rolling time backtests; refresh approved models and show changing uncertainty. Track the specific business outcome: Forecast resilience; avoided emergency borrowing.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Track forecast error and interval coverage by horizon; separate forecast quality from the benefit of the action chosen.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Failure handling:** Never infer guaranteed inflows, move cash or cancel contracts without authority; show downside and restricted funds. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.

**Business outcome:** Forecast error by horizon, missed obligations and financing cost; no sales-growth claim.

**Evaluation:** Measure forecast error and missed obligations; a financed new order is growth only after fulfilment and costs.

**Razorpay direction:** Existing cash visibility/forecasting; validate scenario completeness and decision support rather than recreate a cash dashboard.

**Reuse limitation:** Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. ## 10.7.3 — Currency movements change the margin between quoting and settlement

**Approach:** Predictive ML + workflow · Adjacent / new workflow
**Family:** FAM-64 — International net receipts and FX

**Candidate models:** Seasonal baseline → exponential smoothing or boosted-tree quantiles
**Deep learning:** Deep sequence models are a later option only if extensive diverse history beats simple baselines; small merchants rarely justify training one from scratch.
**Training data:** Consistent dated series, multiple relevant cycles, calendar effects, known commitments and past-only regressors. Stockouts or missing data must not be treated as zero demand.
**Features:** Usable reserves, near-term liabilities, provider exposure, FX obligations and verified terms.
**Target:** Constrained liquidity allocation or transparent finance/FX comparison. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Realized FX variance; margin after conversion costs.
**Agent choice:** Model with a fixed workflow; agent optional. A prediction or ranking can feed a predetermined review-and-action path. Model uncertainty alone does not require an autonomous planner.

### Proposed end-to-end flow

1. Observe: Invoice currencies; timing; supplier payables; quoted FX rates.
2. Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Usable reserves, near-term liabilities, provider exposure, FX obligations and verified terms.
3. Assess: Seasonal naive forecast plus merchant-entered scenario assumptions. Candidate target: Constrained liquidity allocation or transparent finance/FX comparison. Use Seasonal baseline → exponential smoothing or boosted-tree quantiles only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.
4. Recommend: A finance/treasury comparison showing reserves, obligations, terms and explicit unresolved risks. Specific need: Estimate net exposure and compare permitted currency-conversion choices.
5. Review / change / approve: Review liquidity constraints and verified terms; edit reserves/exposure; approve any finance transaction separately.
6. Execute: present the analysis or draft; a person initiates any external action in the appropriate system.
7. Observe the outcome: Realized FX variance; margin after conversion costs. Report this operational, cost or cash outcome separately from sales growth. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.

**Tools to connect:** Read balances/obligations/verified terms; calculate scenarios; prepare a comparison for an authorised human decision.

**Merchant controls:** Review liquidity constraints and verified terms; edit reserves/exposure; approve any finance transaction separately.

**Stopping:** Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).

**Learning:** Compare forecast with realised values through rolling time backtests; refresh approved models and show changing uncertainty. Track the specific business outcome: Realized FX variance; margin after conversion costs.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.

**Accuracy:** Track forecast error and interval coverage by horizon; separate forecast quality from the benefit of the action chosen.

**Permissions:** Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.

**Trust:** Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

**Evaluation:** Measure net costs, liquidity and risk against stated constraints; investment yield is not merchant-sales growth.
